newsitem.title: UK: Hardy says 1997 market conditions difficult.
newsitem.headline: Hardy says 1997 market conditions difficult.

text.p: Lloyd's of London insurance company Hardy Underwriting Group Plc on Thursday warned current market conditions were difficult and it expected income for the 1997 underwriting year to fall considerably from earlier year levels.
But the company said that risks being written were still satisfactory.
The comments were made as the group posted an increase in pre-tax profits for the year to January 31 to 293,000 stg, up from 121,00 stg in 1996.

The company was formed at the end of last year to acquire Hardy Underwriting Agencies, the managing agent of syndicate 382, creating a group which both acts as a small insurance firm and invests in equities and other instruments.
The 1997 profits reflect the investment return and share of profit commission for the 1994 underwriting account from Hardy Underwriting but does not include profits from Syndicate 382.
Profits from the syndicate will, however, be included in next year's results.
Hardy's shares which trade on the alternative investment market (AIM) were unchanged in late afternoon at 155 pence.
In April, syndicate 382 reported profits of 12.3 million stg for the 1994 year, 19 percent of capacity.

Commenting on the performance and outlook for Syndicate 382, Hardy said the 1995 underwriting year was another year of favourable conditions and forecast profit ranging between 20 and 25 percent of capacity of 69.42 million stg.
In 1996 the syndicate reduced capacity by 10 percent in response to weaker markets in some classes.
In 1995 Hardy provided seven percent of underwriting capacity and just over nine percent in 1996.
Hardy's will provide just under one quarter or 16 million stg capacity for the 1997 year of account.
Just over half the syndicate's capacity is aviation with a specialist line in helicopter coverage. It also has a large non-marine book.

Hardy chairman Nigel Ellis said the company was studying a number of ways by which it might benefit from the changes taking place in the market since last year's Lloyd's Reconstruction and Renewal(R&R) programme was implemented.
